deep.reconstruction:
The page is one coherent computation: the Landen–Gauss quadratic transformation of the elliptic integral of the first kind, recast as Gauss's arithmetic-geometric-mean (AGM) algorithm.

(A) Algebraic form. Riemann writes k' for the complementary modulus. The identities below require k'^2 = 1 - k^2; he wrote k' = 1 - kk, which is a slip or a dropped square. Put A = (1+k')/2 and B = (1-k')/2, so that A^2 - B^2 = k' and 4AB = k^2. The substitution is
  1/x = A/y + B y.
Squaring gives
  1/x^2 = A^2/y^2 + B^2 y^2 + 2AB = A^2/y^2 + B^2 y^2 + k^2/2.
Hence
  1/x^2 - k^2 = (A/y - B y)^2,
  1/x^2 - 1 = (1/y^2 - 1)(A^2 - B^2 y^2).
Implicit step (mine): put u = 1/x and v = 1/y. Then dx/sqrt((1-x^2)(1-k^2x^2)) = -du/sqrt((u^2-1)(u^2-k^2)). From u = Av + B/v we get du = (A - B/v^2) dv and sqrt(u^2 - k^2) = (A - B/v^2) v, so du/sqrt(u^2-k^2) = dv/v. This yields the top-line equation
  dx/sqrt((1-x^2)(1-k^2x^2)) = dy/sqrt((1-y^2)(A^2 - B^2 y^2)).
The right side is (2/(1+k')) times a first-kind differential with the smaller modulus (1-k')/(1+k'). This is the descending Landen/Gauss transformation.
The marginal note 'x | sin t, y | sin t'' announces the trigonometric substitution x = sin t, y = sin t'.

(B) Trigonometric/AGM form. Set k' = n/m, so k^2 sin^2 t gives 1 - k^2 sin^2 t = (m^2 cos^2 t + n^2 sin^2 t)/m^2 =: Delta^2/m^2. Then A = (m+n)/(2m) and B = (m-n)/(2m), and the substitution becomes
  1/sin t = ((m+n)/2m)/sin t' + ((m-n)/2m) sin t'.
Equivalently, sin t = 2m sin t'/((m+n) + (m-n) sin^2 t'), which is exactly Gauss's 1818 substitution.
With m' = (m+n)/2 and n' = sqrt(mn) one has A^2 = m'^2/m^2 and A^2 - B^2 = n'^2/m^2. So A^2 - B^2 sin^2 t' = Delta'^2/m^2, and (A) becomes
  J = ∫_0^t dt/sqrt(m^2 cos^2 t + n^2 sin^2 t) = ∫_0^{t'} dt'/sqrt(m'^2 cos^2 t' + n'^2 sin^2 t').
Riemann iterates: m'' = (m'+n')/2, n'' = sqrt(m'n'), and so on. Both sequences tend to the common limit mu = AGM(m,n). With theta = lim t^(k), the integral becomes ∫_0^theta dθ/sqrt(mu^2 cos^2 + mu^2 sin^2) = theta/mu.
One checks t = π/2 maps to t' = π/2, so the complete integral is π/(2 mu) (implicit).

(C) Amplitude relation. From 1/x^2 - 1 = (1/y^2 - 1)(A^2 - B^2 y^2) one gets
  cot^2 t = cot^2 t' · Delta'^2/m^2, i.e. tan t = tan t' · m/Delta'.
Iterating gives tan t = (m/Delta')(m'/Delta'') tan t'', which lets theta be computed from t.

(D) Delta' in terms of Delta. Adding the two square-root identities:
  1/x + sqrt(1/x^2 - k^2) = 2A/y = (1+k')/y.
Also
  sqrt(1/x^2 - k^2) + k'/x = A(1+k')/y - B(1-k') y = 2(A^2/y - B^2 y).
In trigonometric terms (sqrt(1/x^2 - k^2) = Delta/(m sin t)) these read:
  (m + Delta)/(m sin t) = 2m'/(m sin t'),
  (Delta + n)/(m sin t) = 2 Delta'^2/(m^2 sin t').
Dividing gives
  (Delta+n)/(Delta+m) = (Delta'^2/m^2)(m/m'),
hence
  Delta' = sqrt(m m'(Delta+n)/(Delta+m)).
Checks: at t = 0, Delta' = m'; at t = π/2, Delta' = n'.

Purpose: an efficient numerical or algebraic evaluation of the incomplete and complete elliptic integral of the first kind via the AGM, together with the recursion for the amplitude.
errors: The header 'k' = 1 - kk' must be k'^2 = 1 - kk; the term +k^2/2 and all subsequent identities hold only with k'^2 = 1 - k^2. This is a slip of the pen, or a lost exponent in reading.

The line read as 'cot t = cot t' ... Delta'^2/m^2' is correct only as cot^2 t = cot^2 t' Delta'^2/m^2, i.e. cot t = cot t' Delta'/m. Riemann partly struck it and replaced it with the correct tg t = tg t' m/Delta'.

In the line 'sqrt(1/xx - kk) + k'/x = 2(A^2/y) - (B^2) y' the factor 2 must multiply both terms: the correct right side is 2(A^2/y - B^2 y). This is presumably what is meant; the bracket is ambiguous.
Not an error but unstated: theta = lim t^(n) is not identified explicitly, and the complete case (t = π/2 giving t' = π/2, so J = π/(2 mu)) is left implicit.

results.what: Quadratic substitution 1/x = (1+k')/2 · 1/y + (1-k')/2 · y transforming dx/sqrt((1-x^2)(1-k^2x^2)) into dy/sqrt((1-y^2)(A^2-B^2y^2))
results.modern_name: Landen (descending Gauss) transformation of the elliptic integral of the first kind
results.usually_credited_to: Landen 1775, Lagrange 1784, Legendre; Gauss (1799 notes, published 1818)

results.what: Invariance of ∫dt/sqrt(m^2cos^2t+n^2sin^2t) under m→(m+n)/2, n→sqrt(mn), with 1/sin t = (m+n)/(2m)/sin t' + (m-n)/(2m) sin t'; iteration to J = θ/μ
results.modern_name: Gauss's arithmetic-geometric mean evaluation of elliptic integrals

results.what: Amplitude recursion tan t = tan t' m/Δ' and Δ' = sqrt(m m'(Δ+n)/(Δ+m))
results.modern_name: Recursion for the amplitude in the descending Landen/AGM algorithm (cf. modern AGM algorithms for incomplete F(φ,k))
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss 1818 (same notation m, n, μ), Legendre's Traité

deep.surprise_reason: This is a student-style rederivation of Gauss's 1818 AGM treatment, even in Gauss's notation (m, n, m', n', μ), plus the classical Landen transformation. It is correct and neatly done but entirely standard for the period. It shows Riemann working through Gauss's elliptic-integral methods early, which is unsurprising given his background.

(Δ+n)/(Δ+m) = Δ'^2/(m m'), i.e. Δ' = sqrt(m m'(Δ+n)/(Δ+m)) (result 0; may need numeric substitution e.g. m=3,n=1,s=1/2)

transcription_corrections: Header 'k'=1-kk': the formulas require k'^2 = 1-kk. Either Riemann's slip or an exponent missed in transcription.
Marginal 'y | sin t_EV[?]' is most likely 'y | sin t'' (y = sin t'), paired with 'x | sin t'.
Line read as '(1/x)·sqrt(1/xx - kk) + k'/x = ...': the leading symbol is a struck-out character, not 1/x. The identity is sqrt(1/xx - kk) + k'/x = 2[((1+k')/2)^2/y - ((1-k')/2)^2 y].
The line '(1/xx - 1) = (1/yy - 1)(...)' has a struck-out prefix symbol at the left that is not part of the equation.
'cot t = cot t' [-...-] Δ'^2/m^2' is a partly struck line; the intended relation is cot^2 t = cot^2 t' Δ'^2/m^2.
Under the second integral, '[-Δt-] Δ'' labels the radicand of the t'-integral as Δ' (struck 'Δt' or 'Δ'' first attempt).
The line '(1/xx) = ...' originally began with struck '(xx...)'; the intended left side is 1/xx.
